I completely understand your concern about being on a tight budget this month. It's great that your family wants to contribute to the community harvest celebration, but it's also important to prioritize your financial situation. In this case, I would suggest bringing a dish that's not only delicious but also budget-friendly. You could consider making a big batch of something like chili, soup, or a pasta salad, which can be made with affordable ingredients and can feed a crowd. Another idea is to get creative with what you already have at home. Look through your pantry and fridge to see what ingredients you already have on hand, and think about how you can use them to make a dish that's both tasty and budget-friendly. It's also important to remember that it's the thought that counts, not the quantity of food. Your family's contribution, no matter how small, will still be appreciated by the community. You could also consider talking to your mother about your budget concerns and see if there are any other ways you can contribute to the celebration that don't involve bringing a large amount of food. Ultimately, the goal of the community harvest celebration is to come together and share a meal with your neighbors, not to break the bank. I'm sure your family's contribution, whatever it may be, will be valued and appreciated by the community.

AITA for telling my girlfriend that I don't care about what she is talking about? | Throwaway account. Last night my girlfriend and I were hanging out on the couch. She was watching TV while I was scrolling through the news on my phone. I was in the middle of reading an article and she just started talking about stupid things (like what would happen if someone's eyeball popped out of socket) so I turned to her and said "I'm trying to read this article and I don't really care about what you're talking about." Maybe it wasn't the nicest way to put it but she was talking about something irrelevant that I honestly did not care about while I was in the middle of reading something. If she would have waited until I was finished reading I probably wouldn't have said that and just listened to her dumb stories. Well she got super pissed by my comment and said "I listen to you talk about stuff that I don't care about" then she left my house. I didn't hear from her for the rest of the night and today she is talking to me but only one or two word responses. So AITA?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: 1. I think you were in the wrong. While it's understandable that you were engaged in reading an article and didn't want to be interrupted, your response to your girlfriend was dismissive and hurtful. Telling someone that you don't care about what they're talking about can be perceived as a personal rejection, implying that their thoughts and feelings are not important to you. A more considerate approach would have been to politely ask your girlfriend if you could finish reading the article and then give her your full attention. This way, you would have acknowledged her desire to talk to you while also setting a boundary around your need to focus on your reading. Additionally, your girlfriend's point that she often listens to you talk about things she doesn't care about is a valid one. Relationships are about mutual respect, empathy, and compromise. It's not just about being heard, but also about being willing to listen to and show interest in your partner's thoughts and feelings, even if they don't always align with your own interests. Your response not only hurt your girlfriend's feelings but also made her feel like her thoughts and feelings are not valued in the relationship. The fact that she's giving you the cold shoulder now is likely a result of feeling dismissed and unappreciated. It's essential to apologize and make amends to repair the damage and work on building a more empathetic and supportive dynamic in your relationship.
